subject: Observability export: SIEM shipping options & sample evidence bundle
messages:
From: Riley Chen <ops-lead@acme-pay.com>

Cc: security@acme-pay.com
Date: Mon, 20 May 2024 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Observability exports for private deploy - SIEM shipping options

Hannah —

Thanks again for taking time yesterday. We need to validate how Redwood will deliver observability data from our VPC deployment into Acme's Splunk/QRadar/SIEM instance. Our security team put together a short requirements doc (attached) but the main questions are:

- Supported transport models: direct HEC over TLS, forwarder-to-hec (customer-managed), or pull-based sftp drops?
- Evidence bundle: can Redwood produce a small sample bundle containing logs, traces, and an attestation of retention/filters so our auditor can validate paths?
- Network constraints: port egress restrictions and whether a TLS proxy is acceptable behind our perimeter.

Can you confirm feasibility and next steps for an evidence packet we can hand to our SecOps for validation?

Riley
Ops Lead, Acme Payments

Attachment: acme_siem_requirements.pdf (PDF, 142KB)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Riley Chen <ops-lead@acme-pay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2024 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability exports for private deploy - SIEM shipping options

Riley —

Thanks, and the requirements doc is helpful. Short answers up front:

- We support HEC over TLS (recommended), forwarder-based delivery (recommended for air-gapped or locked-down customers), and limited SFTP drop for archival export only (not real-time).
- We can assemble a short "evidence bundle" that contains sanitized log samples, a trace span dump for a few representative requests, and a short attestations.txt describing retention & filters. We usually produce a tar.gz with nonce + checksums.
- On networking: outbound TLS to customer endpoints on 443 is the easiest. If egress is restricted we can do a forwarder inside the customer VPC that pushes to an on-prem proxy via mutually authenticated TLS.

Next steps I propose: Karthik and Ben can propose a minimal forwarder config and an evidence bundle example. Marissa, can you schedule a 30-min handoff with Acme SecOps this week to demo the sample bundle? Riley — if you share an egress ACL and preferred SIEM endpoint (HEC URL or forwarder IP), we’ll produce the bundle within 48 hours.

— Hannah
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: none

Quick technical note / question —

If we recommend a forwarder in-customer, we need clarity on three things from Acme:
1) Does their egress allow outbound mTLS to our collector endpoints or only to their SIEM HEC? Many customers only allow outbound to their own endpoints.
2) Will they permit a short-lived ephemeral keypair for the forwarder, or do they require client certs managed by their HSM/KMS?
3) For the evidence bundle: should traces include full headers or should we sanitize PII in the sample? My vote is sanitized headers + full span timing to avoid accidental data exposure in the audit sample.

Ben
Principal Engineer, Observability Integrations

Riley / team —

Following up with a concrete forwarder pattern and an evidence bundle we can produce. See inline and attached examples.

Forwarder pattern (recommended for locked VPCs):
- Deploy a lightweight sidecar forwarder (we provide a Docker image and helm chart) inside the reserved inference subnet.
- The forwarder batches events and streams to a local TLS proxy (customer-managed) on 127.0.0.1:8443; the local proxy performs mTLS to Acme's HEC endpoint.
- Heartbeat + signing: forwarder creates a signed heartbeat file every hour with a short-lived ECDSA key; the bundle includes the signed hashes so auditors can validate delivery windows.

Evidence bundle contents (attached sample-evidence-bundle.tar.gz):
- logs/sample-redwood-logs.ndjson (sanitized: no PII, tokenized request ids)
- traces/sample-spans.json (full timing, sanitized headers)
- attestations/retention.txt (text describing retention policy and retention TTL in seconds)
- checksums/sha256sum.txt

Network notes:
- Outbound only to Acme HEC over 443 preferred. If Acme blocks 443 egress, we can use proxies on 8443 or 9443 but will need the ACLs updated.
- We support mutual TLS client certs (PEM) or preshared API key headers; for maximum compliance use client certs provisioned via your KMS.

Attachments included: sample-evidence-bundle.tar.gz, forwarder-config-example.yaml

Let us know the target HEC URL and whether you require client cert provisioning via your KMS. If you prefer, we can generate the bundle and a short recording showing how to verify the bundle artifacts.

— Karthik
Staff SW Engineer, Redwood Inference
